questions.question: Which group of viruses infects bacterial cells?
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages ("bacteria eaters") are viruses whose hosts are bacteria; viroids and prions are not viruses and mycoplasmas are bacteria.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is a plant virus with which type of genome?
questions.explanation: TMV is a helical virus whose genome is a single strand of RNA enclosed in a protein capsid.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: What name is given to the protein coat that surrounds the nucleic acid of a virus?
questions.explanation: The capsid is made of protein subunits called capsomeres and protects the viral genome.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Which virus shows complex symmetry, having a polyhedral head joined to a helical tail?
questions.explanation: T4 phage has an icosahedral head and a helical tail with tail fibres; TMV is purely helical and adenovirus is purely icosahedral.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Which virus–genome pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Poliovirus has a positive-sense ssRNA genome; herpes viruses carry dsDNA, hepatitis B has a partly double-stranded DNA genome and influenza has segmented ssRNA.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: A virus particle has a lipid membrane with glycoprotein spikes outside its nucleocapsid. How is such a virus described?
questions.explanation: The envelope is acquired from the host membrane as the virus buds out, and distinguishes enveloped from naked viruses.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Bacteriophage, tobacco mosaic virus and HIV are placed in separate categories mainly on the basis of which criterion?
options: The type of host they infect
questions.explanation: Hosts (bacteria, plants and humans respectively) are one of the classification criteria for viruses.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: A virus has a single-stranded RNA genome and carries reverse transcriptase in its virion. To which group does it belong?
questions.explanation: Retroviruses copy RNA into DNA using reverse transcriptase before integrating into host DNA; HIV is an example.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Which list contains only diseases caused by viruses?
questions.explanation: Measles, mumps and rabies are viral; the second list is bacterial, the third protozoal and the fourth fungal.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Why are viruses not placed in any of the five kingdoms of living organisms?
options: They contain both DNA and RNA
They are acellular and can reproduce only inside host cells
They have ribosomes but no cell membrane
questions.explanation: Viruses lack cellular organization and metabolic machinery and are obligate intracellular parasites; each virion contains either DNA or RNA, never both.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.1

questions.question: Which agent causes AIDS?
questions.explanation: AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) is the late stage of infection by HIV.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which cells does HIV primarily infect and destroy?
questions.explanation: HIV binds the CD4 receptor, so helper T cells are its main targets, weakening the immune response.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which activity can transmit HIV from an infected to an uninfected person?
questions.explanation: HIV spreads through blood, sexual fluids and breast milk, not through casual contact.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which enzyme enables HIV to make a DNA copy of its RNA genome inside the host cell?
questions.explanation: Reverse transcriptase synthesizes DNA from the viral RNA template, which integrates into the host chromosome.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Why do people with advanced AIDS often die of infections that rarely harm healthy people?
options: HIV directly digests the tissues of the lungs
The patients lose all their red blood cells
Loss of helper T cells cripples the immune response, allowing opportunistic infections
HIV converts harmless bacteria into toxins
questions.explanation: Opportunistic pathogens take advantage of the profound immune deficiency caused by helper T-cell depletion.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which combination of features is typical of advanced HIV infection?
options: High fever with a rash that lasts three days only
Sudden paralysis with loss of vision
Yellowing of skin with dark urine only
Persistent swollen lymph nodes, weight loss and recurrent opportunistic infections
questions.explanation: Chronic lymphadenopathy, wasting and repeated opportunistic infections characterize progression to AIDS.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: By which route can an HIV-positive mother pass the virus to her baby?
options: Across the placenta, during delivery or through breast milk
Only through the baby's blood group antigens
questions.explanation: Mother-to-child (vertical) transmission can occur in pregnancy, at birth or while breastfeeding.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which illness is considered an opportunistic infection that is often linked with AIDS?
questions.explanation: Pneumocystis jirovecii causes severe pneumonia mostly in people with markedly low CD4 counts.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: A person infected with HIV a fortnight ago tests negative for HIV antibodies. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The test was done in the window period before antibodies were produced
The test detects only bacterial proteins
questions.explanation: Antibodies take weeks to appear after infection, so an early antibody test can be falsely negative.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Which property of HIV makes it difficult to develop an effective vaccine?
options: Its inability to enter any cell
Rapid mutation of its genome, producing antigenic variation
questions.explanation: Reverse transcriptase lacks proofreading, so many variants arise and the virus escapes the immune response.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 1.2

questions.question: Into which small molecules are dietary proteins digested before they can be used in respiration?
questions.explanation: Proteins are hydrolysed to amino acids, some of which are oxidised for energy.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: What are the products of hydrolysis of a triglyceride?
questions.explanation: Lipases split a triglyceride into one glycerol and three fatty acids.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: Which two-carbon unit is produced when fatty acids are broken down by beta-oxidation?
questions.explanation: Beta-oxidation successively removes two-carbon fragments as acetyl CoA.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: What happens to an amino acid before its carbon skeleton can enter the respiratory pathway?
options: It is converted into glucose in the mitochondria
Its carboxyl group is joined to glycerol
It is polymerised into a protein
questions.explanation: Deamination removes the amino group as ammonia, which the liver converts to urea; the remaining keto acid enters respiration.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: At which point does glycerol from fat breakdown enter the respiratory pathway?
options: Directly as acetyl CoA in the Krebs cycle
As a triose phosphate in glycolysis
questions.explanation: Glycerol is phosphorylated and converted to a triose phosphate (glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate), an intermediate of glycolysis.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: Compared with an equal mass of carbohydrate, complete oxidation of fat yields
options: Less energy, because fats contain more oxygen
The same energy, since both give acetyl CoA
No energy unless converted to glucose first
More energy, because fats are richer in reduced C-H bonds
questions.explanation: Fats are more reduced than carbohydrates, so they release about twice as much energy per gram.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: Where does beta-oxidation of fatty acids mainly take place in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Fatty acids are activated in the cytoplasm and oxidised in the mitochondrial matrix, where the Krebs cycle also operates.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: The respiratory quotient (RQ) is the ratio of CO2 released to O2 consumed. What RQ is expected when only carbohydrate is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Oxidation of glucose releases 6 CO2 for 6 O2 consumed; fats give about 0.7 because they contain little oxygen.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: How many acetyl CoA molecules are formed from complete beta-oxidation of one 16-carbon fatty acid such as palmitic acid?
questions.explanation: Each acetyl CoA contains two carbons, so a C16 chain gives eight of them after seven rounds of beta-oxidation.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: Which molecule is the common entry point to the Krebs cycle for carbon skeletons from glucose, fatty acids and many amino acids?
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA is the convergence point where carbohydrate, lipid and protein catabolism merge before entering the Krebs cycle.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 2.1

questions.question: Which set lists the four major classes of biological macromolecules?
options: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids are the four main organic macromolecule classes of cells.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which element forms the backbone of all organic biological molecules?
questions.explanation: Carbon forms the skeleton of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which of the following is a small monomer-type biomolecule rather than a macromolecule?
questions.explanation: An amino acid is a single building block; haemoglobin, glycogen and DNA are large polymers.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which property of carbon makes it suitable as the framework of biological molecules?
options: It readily forms ionic bonds with all metals
It exists only as a gas at body temperature
It is tetravalent and forms stable covalent bonds in chains and rings
It has no tendency to bond with other carbon atoms
questions.explanation: Four valence electrons let carbon form four covalent bonds, including long chains, branches and rings.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which monomer–polymer pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Nucleotides polymerise to form DNA and RNA; amino acids form proteins and glucose forms starch, cellulose and glycogen.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which biomolecule class is not a true polymer built from repeating monomer units?
questions.explanation: Lipids are assembled from different components such as glycerol and fatty acids and are not chains of repeated monomers.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which of these is an inorganic biological molecule?
questions.explanation: Water lacks a carbon skeleton, whereas the other three are organic compounds.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: What type of reaction joins monomers to build a polymer, and what small molecule does it release?
questions.explanation: Dehydration synthesis removes a water molecule at each new bond formed.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which macromolecule class always contains phosphorus in each of its monomers?
questions.explanation: Each nucleotide includes a phosphate group; proteins, polysaccharides and triglycerides lack phosphate in their basic monomers.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: A compound analysis shows only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 1:2:1. To which class does the compound most likely belong?
questions.explanation: The empirical formula (CH2O)n is characteristic of carbohydrates.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.1

questions.question: Which biomolecule is the main immediate source of energy for cells?
questions.explanation: Cells oxidise glucose in respiration to produce ATP quickly.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which class of biomolecules acts as biological catalysts?
questions.explanation: Nearly all enzymes are proteins that speed up metabolic reactions.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which molecule stores hereditary information in cells?
questions.explanation: The sequence of bases in DNA encodes genetic information.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which role is performed by lipids but not by carbohydrates?
options: Forming the bilayer of cell membranes
Serving as the main store of liver energy
questions.explanation: Phospholipids form the structural bilayer of all cell membranes.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Why do animals store most of their long-term energy as fat rather than glycogen?
options: Fat is more energy-dense and is stored without much associated water
Fat is a polymer of glucose
questions.explanation: Fat holds more energy per gram and is hydrophobic, so it is stored compactly.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which nucleotide-derived molecule acts as the immediate energy currency of the cell?
questions.explanation: ATP links energy-releasing reactions with energy-requiring ones.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which biomolecule provides mechanical strength to the plant cell wall?
questions.explanation: Cellulose microfibrils give tensile strength to plant cell walls.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Lipids in the diet are necessary mainly for the absorption of which vitamins?
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and are absorbed with dietary lipids.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which molecule is the precursor of steroid hormones such as testosterone and oestrogen?
questions.explanation: Steroid hormones are synthesised from the lipid cholesterol.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: Which function is carried out mainly by proteins rather than by carbohydrates or lipids?
options: Storing energy in muscles as glycogen
Insulating the body against heat loss
questions.explanation: Enzymatic catalysis is the characteristic role of protein molecules.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.2

questions.question: What term describes a molecule like water that has unequal sharing of electrons, giving partial charges?
questions.explanation: Oxygen attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen, so water has a partially negative O and partially positive H atoms.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Which type of bond forms between neighbouring water molecules?
questions.explanation: The partially positive H of one water molecule attracts the partially negative O of another.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Why does ice float on liquid water?
options: Ice is heavier than liquid water
Ice is less dense than liquid water
questions.explanation: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open lattice, making it less dense than liquid water.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Which property of water lets columns of water be pulled up the xylem without breaking?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding makes water molecules cohere, supporting continuous columns in transpiration pull.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Why are large water bodies stable habitats with small temperature changes?
options: Water has a very low boiling point
Water conducts heat poorly as a gas
Water has a high specific heat capacity
questions.explanation: A large amount of heat is needed to raise water's temperature, which buffers aquatic organisms.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Why do NaCl crystals dissolve readily in water?
options: Water molecules surround Na+ and Cl- ions and separate them
Water forms covalent bonds with sodium
Water neutralises the ions into atoms
questions.explanation: Polar water molecules form hydration shells around ions, pulling the lattice apart.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: In the digestion of sucrose to glucose and fructose, how does water participate?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis uses a water molecule to break a glycosidic bond.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: Evaporation of sweat cools the skin because water has a high
questions.explanation: Much heat energy is absorbed to break hydrogen bonds when water vaporises, so heat leaves the body.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: In pure water at 25 °C, what is the concentration of H+ ions due to ionisation?
questions.explanation: Water ionises slightly into H+ and OH-, giving [H+] = 10^-7 M and pH 7 at 25 °C.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: In photosynthesis, water acts as a reagent by providing
options: Electrons and protons, with release of oxygen
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water supplies electrons and H+ to the light reactions and releases O2.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.3

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a hexose monosaccharide with six carbons.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Which two monosaccharides combine to form sucrose?
questions.explanation: Sucrose (cane sugar) is a disaccharide made of glucose and fructose.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Which polysaccharide is the main storage carbohydrate of animals?
questions.explanation: Glycogen is stored in liver and muscles of animals.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Which sugar is made of glucose and galactose?
questions.explanation: Lactose, the milk sugar, is a disaccharide of glucose and galactose.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: How do amylose and amylopectin, the two components of starch, differ?
options: Amylose is made of fructose while amylopectin is made of glucose
Amylose is unbranched while amylopectin is branched
Amylose is a protein while amylopectin is a lipid
Amylose is found in animals while amylopectin is found in plants
questions.explanation: Both are glucose polymers, but amylopectin has alpha-1,6 branch points.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Humans cannot digest cellulose mainly because
options: It is made of amino acids
It is insoluble in all solvents
It has beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds that our enzymes cannot hydrolyse
questions.explanation: Humans lack cellulase to break beta-1,4 linkages between glucose units.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: How does glycogen structurally differ from starch's amylopectin?
questions.explanation: Glycogen has more frequent branch points, allowing rapid release of glucose.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Which sugar gives a negative Benedict's test before hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: In sucrose both anomeric carbons are involved in the glycosidic bond, so it has no free reducing group.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: What kind of bond joins the two glucose units in maltose?
questions.explanation: Maltose consists of two alpha-glucose units linked by an alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Why do cellulose fibres have high tensile strength?
options: Chains are coiled into helices like starch
Chains are branched at every glucose
Parallel chains are cross-linked by hydrogen bonds into microfibrils
Chains are joined by disulfide bridges
questions.explanation: Alternate glucose units are inverted, so straight chains lie side by side and form hydrogen-bonded microfibrils.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.4

questions.question: Which groups are attached to the central carbon of every amino acid?
options: Phosphate group, sugar and a base
Amino group, carboxyl group, hydrogen and an R group
Hydroxyl group, glycerol and a fatty acid
Aldehyde group, ketone group and an ester
questions.explanation: The alpha carbon bears NH2, COOH, H and a variable R group.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Which bond joins two amino acids together?
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: What does the primary structure of a protein refer to?
options: The folding of the whole chain
questions.explanation: Primary structure is the linear order of amino acids in the polypeptide.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Which bonds mainly stabilise the alpha helix and beta pleated sheet?
questions.explanation: Secondary structure depends on hydrogen bonding between the C=O and N-H groups of the backbone.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: The tertiary structure of a protein is held by interactions between
questions.explanation: Disulfide, ionic, hydrophobic and hydrogen interactions among R groups fold the chain into its 3-D shape.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Why is haemoglobin said to have a quaternary structure?
options: It consists of four polypeptide chains
questions.explanation: Quaternary structure is the assembly of two or more polypeptide subunits; haemoglobin has two alpha and two beta chains.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Which statement describes an amino acid at neutral pH?
options: It is always neutral with no charges
It carries only a positive charge
It carries only a negative charge
It exists as a zwitterion carrying both positive and negative charges
questions.explanation: The amino group is protonated and the carboxyl group is deprotonated, forming a dipolar ion.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Sickle-cell haemoglobin arises from which change in the beta chain?
options: Glutamic acid replaced by valine at position 6
Valine replaced by glutamic acid at position 6
Replacement of a peptide bond by an ester bond
questions.explanation: A single amino acid substitution alters the primary structure and causes haemoglobin S to polymerise.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Disulfide bridges form between the R groups of which amino acid?
questions.explanation: Cysteine contains a thiol (-SH) group and two such groups oxidise to a disulfide bond.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: Moderate heating of egg white denatures its proteins. Which level of structure is NOT broken?
questions.explanation: Heat disrupts weak bonds that maintain higher-order structure but leaves covalent peptide bonds of the primary structure intact.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.5

questions.question: What is the basic composition of a triglyceride?
options: Three glycerol and one fatty acid
One glycerol and three fatty acids
questions.explanation: A triglyceride is a glycerol joined to three fatty acids by ester bonds.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.6

questions.question: Phospholipids are described as amphipathic because they have
options: A hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails
questions.explanation: The phosphate-containing head is water-loving and the fatty acid tails are water-repelling.
questions.subject: biology
questions.source_reference: MDCAT Arena original item; independently authored against PM&DC MDCAT 2025 syllabus SLO 3.6

questions.question: Which feature identifies a saturated fatty acid?
options: One or more double bonds in its chain
A phosphate group on the chain
An amino group on the chain
No carbon-carbon double bonds in its chain
questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids have the maximum number of hydrogens and no C=C double bonds.
